fields.v: Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — time-consistent PR-based benchmark protocol with a matched A/B design for repository-knowledge augmentation; baseline-only characterization comparing four prompt granularities x three Claude models on two repositories

rev.why: Form fixed to '<nature>; secondary: <nature> — <detail>'. Secondary changed from 'evaluates' to 'Compares' because the characterization study contrasts prompt levels and models; 'Evaluates' is also defensible since no approach is the object and no baseline arm exists

Main nature is clear (benchmark protocol = evaluation method). Secondary 'Compares' (prompt levels x models) vs 'Evaluates' is a judgement: no approach is the object and the planned baseline-vs-augmented comparison is not run

fields.warn: A principal (protocolo de benchmark) é clara. Decide se a secundária é 'Compares' (níveis de prompt × modelos) ou 'Evaluates': nenhuma abordagem é o objeto e a comparação baseline vs. aumentado não é executada.

fields.v: No SDD approach. Object of the protocol: repository-derived code knowledge layer (not evaluated here). Varied factor in the study: task prompt granularity (Minimal, Concise, Contextual, Guided) generated by an LLM from historical PRs

Natural-language task prompts derived from PRs at four granularity levels (Minimal: from PR title; Concise: affected component / limited repository grounding; Contextual: functionality/usage/failure mode, without function names or repair instructions; Guided: structured guidance on the fix — described in §3.1 as not exposing the implementation, but in §3.3 as including 'partial implementation hints extracted from the pull request'); repository-derived code knowledge built from snapshot t0 (source, commit history, docs) for the augmented arm

rev.why: The paper defines the levels twice and differently: §3.3 says Guided includes partial implementation hints from the PR, which the value omitted (it gave only the §3.1 'without exposing the implementation' wording)

fields.v: Benchmark protocol: snapshot repository at t0 -> build repository knowledge from pre-t0 artefacts only -> collect PRs merged in (t0, t1] -> LLM converts each PR to a task prompt at granularity l -> run same SWE agent with and without repository knowledge -> compare predicted files with PR-modified files

Criterion: file-level F1 of predicted files vs PR-modified files; baseline arm only (no repository knowledge); agent not stated; one entry per model x prompt level x repository. Quality verdict for every entry: no criterion stated by the authors (the study sets no F1 threshold); cost not measured, so cost verdict N/A for every entry. DragonFly (Table 2), F1 for Minimal / Concise / Contextual / Guided: agent not stated + Claude Sonnet 4: 0.2026 / 0.3916 / 0.5592 / 0.6828; agent not stated + Claude Sonnet 4.5: 0.2487 / 0.4124 / 0.5656 / 0.7163; agent not stated + 'Claude-Ops-4.6' (Opus 4.6): 0.2952 / 0.5464 / 0.7241 / 0.8081. React (Table 3, 90 tasks per condition): Sonnet 4: 0.1898 / 0.3710 / 0.4594 / 0.6283; Sonnet 4.5: 0.1946 / 0.3751 / 0.5062 / 0.7229; Opus 4.6: 0.2335 / 0.5098 / 0.6057 / 0.8078. React averaged over models (Table 4): mean F1 0.242 / 0.479 / 0.574 / 0.770; Precision=0 rate 60.2% / 28.7% / 18.5% / 3.5%; Recall=1 rate 14.4% / 31.1% / 41.5% / 59.8%

rev.why: Section 6 requires a verdict per configuration (model x prompt level x repository) judged on its own; r1 gave one pooled verdict per prompt level ('Guided works', 'Concise partly'), which hides that e.g. Sonnet 4 Guided (0.6828, 0.6283) and Sonnet 4 Concise (0.3916, 0.3710) differ from the other models at the same level. F1 values unchanged (re-checked against Tables 2-4). The F1 cut-offs are the extractor's judgement
Rule 1: removed the extractor's F1 scale (>= 0.70 works, 0.40-0.70 partly, < 0.40 does not work) and the per-entry quality verdicts; the study sets no F1 threshold. All configurations and values kept

fields.v: Baseline characterization: 2 repositories x 3 Claude models x 4 prompt granularities; no knowledge-augmented arm. Held constant (by design): snapshot, task set, environment, metric; agent not named. Acceptance tests: none (file-overlap with ground-truth PR). Repetitions: not stated (apparently 1). Human intervention: not stated

F1 rises monotonically from Minimal to Guided for every model and repository (e.g. DragonFly Opus 4.6 0.2952 -> 0.8081; React Opus 4.6 0.2335 -> 0.8078); stronger models have higher F1 at each granularity, but not higher recall everywhere (DragonFly Sonnet 4.5 recall below Sonnet 4 at Concise, Contextual and Guided; React Sonnet 4.5 below Sonnet 4 at Minimal and Concise). The authors say the largest jump often occurs Concise -> Contextual (said of DragonFly), but Tables 2-3 do not support it: the largest F1 step is Minimal -> Concise in 5 of 6 model-repository rows (DragonFly Sonnet 4.5 steps nearly equal: +0.164 / +0.153 / +0.151) and Contextual -> Guided for React Sonnet 4.5; it is never Concise -> Contextual. No significance tests

rev.why: The value repeated the authors' 'largest jump often Concise -> Contextual' as a result; recomputed from Tables 2 and 3, the largest F1 step is Minimal -> Concise for DragonFly Sonnet 4 (+0.189) and Opus 4.6 (+0.251) and for all React rows except Sonnet 4.5 (Contextual -> Guided +0.217)

r1 said the largest step is never Concise -> Contextual 'on React'; it is never so in any row, including all DragonFly rows, where the authors make the claim. Added that the stronger-model ordering holds for F1 but not for recall (Tables 2-3), which the authors state for 'all three metrics'

fields.warn: O valor contradiz, com base nas Tabelas 2–3, a afirmação dos autores de que o maior salto é Concise → Contextual, e nota que o Sonnet 4.5 tem recall inferior ao Sonnet 4. Confirma esses cálculos nas tabelas.

fields.v: Distinguished prompt granularities and models; the A/B knowledge comparison (main purpose) not yet run. Repeatability: claimed cross-repository consistency; no repetitions or CIs. Limitations stated: no paired augmented-vs-baseline deltas, incomplete uncertainty reporting, prompt templates and leakage filters not given, file-level metric only, two repositories, two DragonFly Concise detail exports missing

Prompt granularity is a first-order benchmark variable; Contextual recommended as default. Gaps: complete matched A/B evaluation with task-level deltas, uncertainty estimates, exact prompt templates, execution-based correctness (patch/test pass), broader repository coverage

Prompt level 'Concise' appears as 'Abstract' in Figures 2-5 and 10. Model 'Claude-Ops-4.6' presumably Claude Opus 4.6 (as written). Table 4 columns Prec.=0 and Rec.=0 have identical values (60.2/28.7/18.5/3.5%), possible reporting error. Task-level analysis (Table 4, Figures 6-7) covers React; DragonFly task count never stated. Claim that the largest jump is often Concise -> Contextual (p. 5) is not supported by Tables 2-3. Claim that stronger models 'consistently improve all three metrics at matched prompt granularity' (p. 5) is contradicted for recall: DragonFly Sonnet 4.5 vs Sonnet 4 at Concise 0.3980 vs 0.4365, Contextual 0.5999 vs 0.6176, Guided 0.7068 vs 0.7314; React Minimal 0.1886 vs 0.1921, Concise 0.3598 vs 0.3989. Prompt levels defined differently in §3.1 and §3.3 (Guided 'avoids direct exposure of the ground-truth implementation' vs 'partial implementation hints extracted from the pull request'), so the claim that prompts do not leak solution-critical information is inconsistent. Tables 2-3 rebuilt from pdftotext order (models x prompts) and cross-checked with the Figure 10a heatmap. The SWE agent used to produce predictions is never named. Threats section refers to 'the current draft'. No data/replication package or pre-registration stated. Languages: not stated (React is JavaScript)
